To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
eudaimonic user experiences (UX) are more meaningful, more long-term, and more related to need fulfilment than hedonic UX.

1. eudaimonic user experiences (UX) can be distinguished from hedonic UX by their focus on striving towards and accomplancing personal goals; 2. eudaimonia is related to hedonia, but also to other established UX dimensions such as need fulfillment, positive emotion, and meaning; 3. eudaimonix experiences are important for users, as they are related to increased long-term importance and satisfaction with technology
Eudaimonic user experiences (UX) are about striving towards and attaining personal goals through technology, while hedonic UX are about momentary pleasure derived directly from technology use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of meaning in technology use.
the question of how to best define and measure the quality of interactive technology.
how technology can be used to enhance the lives of users.

the hedonic is about momentary pleasure and eudaimonic user experiences are about lasting meaning.
eudaimonic and hedonic experiences are two different kinds of user experiences that are not mutually exclusive but rather complementary.

hedonic UX is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for eudaimonic technology use.
the eudaimonics of UX is the experience of meaning from the fulfilment of needs through technology use.
the eudaimonia concept offers an important complement to the hedonia concept in the UX research.

eudaimonic and hedonic UX are distinct and complementary.
